A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AnesSuite/Morpheus study. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison despite pagination and subsection-number changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations, Morpheus training results, ablations, and supplementary experiments in Tables 3–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds an InternLM3 training comparison and quantitative reasoning-hallucination results in Tables 12 and 24.

M1.justification: Dataset construction and the Morpheus SFT-plus-GRPO procedure, including binary outcome rewards and the 32B LoRA configuration, remain unchanged. Applying the existing training procedure to InternLM3 does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The training datasets, bilingual AnesBench tasks, general-domain and medical benchmarks, CAB, and open-ended subset are retained. The new hallucination audit samples existing English System 2 questions; InternLM3 is tested on existing coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.2 adds an InternLM3-8B-Instruct baseline-versus-trained comparison in Table 12. InternLM3 already appeared in v3's benchmark evaluation, but now participates in the training comparison. Existing comparator sets remain unchanged; GPT-OSS-120B serves as the new audit's judge.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce an InternLM3 configuration with 100 SFT and 60 GRPO steps, plus a 50-question hallucination audit using sentence segmentation, coreference resolution, filtering, and GPT-OSS-120B judgments. Previously reported evaluation protocols and Morpheus training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G.3 adds a substantial quantitative error-analysis component: reasoning validity and four hallucination categories across seven models on 50 System 2 questions. This extends v3's selected qualitative cases into a systematic audit. Appendix C.2 also adds a further check of training effectiveness on InternLM3.

E5.justification: Both versions report three Morpheus-7B training runs, three repetitions of open-ended judging, and Appendix F's bootstrap tests, confidence intervals, and correlation tests. The new experiments add no reported uncertainty estimates or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: New Table 12 reports InternLM3 overall accuracy of 0.54 before training and 0.58 afterward. Table 24 newly reports reasoning-validity rates, including 76.2% for Morpheus-7B versus 68.8% for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Existing result tables retain their values. Table 12's per-level InternLM baseline differs from the unchanged Table 9 without explanation.

T1.justification: The leakage-confidence definition in Appendix A.1 and regression formulation in Appendix F.1 are retained. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The dataset-suite, Morpheus, and comprehensive-evaluation contributions retain their meaning and scope. v4 explicitly mentions general-medical and broad-domain transfer in the abstract, but v3 already makes that claim in its introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v4 attributes reasoning failures partly to logical hallucinations and interprets the new audit as evidence of improved safety, suggesting process rewards and retrieval as remedies. It also qualifies uneven generalization and replaces Qwen's vague 'inherent sensitivities' explanation with a possible alignment tax from insufficient SFT. Section 6's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 documents the new audit's spaCy/GPT-OSS-120B processing pipeline and evaluation prompt, and specifies the InternLM training budget. The datasheet now directs users to first-page contact emails instead of promising a future contact address. Existing implementation and release disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references covering GPT-OSS, process reward modeling, RAG/REX-RAG, and multimodal retrieval to support the hallucination discussion. Section 2 and the central positioning against earlier anesthesiology benchmarks remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include localized abstract and discussion revisions, restored text in Case 2 excerpts, new acknowledgements, author/affiliation edits, and the conference-publication header. Datasheet headings become unnumbered, while the overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 12 and 24 and a hallucination-evaluation prompt box. Existing figures remain unchanged; Table 2 and Figures 3–4 move, while appendix tables and prompt/case boxes are repaginated. These are limited additions and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful evidence for AnesR1 training on another foundation model and quantifies reasoning errors beyond v3's selected cases. The disclosed judge prompt and more qualified generalization discussion also help assessment. These gains are limited: the 50-question automated audit lacks reported human validation and uncertainty estimates, weakening its stronger safety interpretation, and the new InternLM comparison leaves a baseline discrepancy between Tables 9 and 12 unexplained.
